findings.finding: The reviewer's findings table could not be read, so its rows are not listed here: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/nfr-requirements/performance-requirements.md: findings table header declares #, Severity, Location, Finding, Recommendation. findings.required_action: Address the reviewer's findings as written below this table.

findings.location: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/nfr-requirements/security-requirements.md > Requirements rows NFR2.3 and NFR2.4, the STRIDE table (Spoofing, Repudiation, Elevation of privilege rows) and the Residual-risk note; also tech-stack-decisions.md > Decisions row "Authentication" and the "Deferred to Infrastructure Design" networking bullet
findings.finding: The security requirements still say there is no caller authentication at MVP and that future auth would be an `X-Api-Key` header. The consumed contract now says the opposite: contract-summary.md sets a global `security: - cognitoJwt: []`, every item route returns 401 from the API Gateway JWT check, and only `/health` is open (`security: []`). The functional design follows the contract (rules.md BR6.1, functional-spec.md WF-AUTH). A reader today who takes the security NFRs as the source would build an unauthenticated service, and the threat table understates what is now mitigated (spoofing by the JWT check, repudiation by a known caller identity). The person accepted this drift at the Contract Design gate and the later design and code already realise auth, so this is a stale-document issue rather than a wrong decision, which is why it is Major and not Critical.
findings.required_action: Revise NFR2.3 to state the binding requirement: every item route needs a valid Cognito user pool JWT bearer token checked at the API Gateway, 401 with the gateway body otherwise, `/health` open, no roles (cite contract Q7, Q8 and BR6.1). Replace NFR2.4 (the `X-Api-Key` seam) with the remaining open items from the contract (token flow and lifetime, admin user creation, decided at Infrastructure Design). Update the Spoofing, Repudiation and Elevation rows and the residual-risk note, and change the tech-stack Authentication row from None to Cognito JWT at the gateway.

findings.location: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/nfr-requirements/security-requirements.md > NFR2.1 Detail; also performance-requirements.md NFR1.4 and scalability-requirements.md NFR1.9
findings.finding: NFR2.1 restates the validation bounds as "quantity non-negative integer; delta non-zero integer; offset at least 0", which is narrower than the current source it cites. rules.md BR4.1 and the contract also require offset at most 10000, quantity at most 9007199254740991, delta within plus or minus 9007199254740991, an increment whose result exceeds 9007199254740991 rejected with 400 (contract Q10, BR2.1), name at most 200 characters and description at most 2000. NFR1.4 and NFR1.9 claim list cost is bounded by limit alone, but an unbounded offset is exactly what the contract cap (Q11) closes. BR4.1 is the stated source of truth, so the gap is a misleading restatement rather than a missing rule.
findings.required_action: Bring the NFR2.1 bounds in line with BR4.1 (add the offset cap, the quantity and delta range, the overflow rejection and the name and description lengths), or replace the restated list with a plain reference to BR4.1. Add the offset cap of 10000 to NFR1.4 and NFR1.9.

findings.location: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/nfr-requirements/observability-requirements.md > NFR3.2 and the SLI/SLO linkage section
findings.finding: NFR3.2 says every request emits one service log entry, and the availability SLI is derived from service logs. Since BR6.1, a 401 request never reaches the service; rules.md BR5.1 says it is recorded instead in the gateway access log. As written, the NFRs do not cover rejected requests, and an availability SLI computed only from service logs leaves out traffic the gateway answered.
findings.required_action: Scope NFR3.2 to requests that reach the service, add a requirement for the gateway access log (requestId, timestamp, method, route, statusCode) per BR5.1, and say which log the availability SLI counts, and whether a 401 counts as a successful request.

findings.finding: NFR1.2 is marked Binding, but its target ("small, e.g. at most 3 internal attempts"; must not "materially inflate perceived latency") has no fixed number and cannot pass or fail a test. The inception guardrails require testable requirements. It also leaves open what the caller gets when retries run out, since `ConcurrencyConflict` is not in the contract's error enum.
findings.required_action: Fix the retry budget as a number (for example exactly 3 attempts) and state the outcome when it is exhausted (for example `InternalError` 500, logged), or mark the latency part Deferred like NFR1.5.

### Validation Tool Results

| Tool | Result | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| traceability.json structure (read and checked by hand) | PASS | Valid JSON with `upstream_ids` NFR1 to NFR4. These match exactly the four NFRs in requirements.md (NFR1 correctness, NFR2 validation, NFR3 observability, NFR4 secrets). Every one is in `coverage` with status OK. |
| Derived ID cross-check (coverage targets against requirement rows) | PASS | NFR1.1 to NFR1.5 (performance), NFR1.6 to NFR1.10 (scalability), NFR1.11 to NFR1.16 (reliability), NFR2.1 to NFR2.5 and NFR4.1 to NFR4.2 (security), NFR3.1 (reliability) and NFR3.2 to NFR3.9 (observability). That is 32 IDs, each defined exactly once, with no dangling target and no orphan row. |
| Deferred rows against `reverse[]` | PASS | The five rows with status Deferred (NFR1.5, NFR1.10, NFR1.16, NFR3.8, NFR3.9) are exactly the five `reverse[]` entries, each with a reason. |
| Measurable targets | PARTIAL | NFR1.11 is measurable (99.9% over a 30-day rolling window, about 43.8 minutes a month, arithmetic correct). NFR1.2 is not (Minor finding above). Other numeric targets are explicitly deferred, consistent with the team's deferral of performance testing. |
| Contract and functional-design consistency | FAIL (auth, validation bounds, 401 logging) | Checked against contract-summary.md (cognitoJwt, offset max 10000, quantity max 9007199254740991, closed error enum) and rules.md BR4.1, BR5.1 and BR6.1. The auth posture contradicts the contract (Major). The validation bounds and the 401 logging lag behind the rules (Minor). The DynamoDB conditional update, the transparent conflict handling and the locked log field set all match. |
| `aidlc engine sensor-traceability` | Not run | This command writes traceability.json through `--output-path`, and this review may write only its review file. The structure was checked by hand instead (rows above). |

### Summary

The NFR set is structurally sound. Traceability is complete and consistent, every inception NFR is covered, deferrals are justified, and the concurrency, datastore and logging decisions match the contract. The one substantive problem is that the reviewed security artifact, and the tech-stack auth row, still describe an unauthenticated API with an `X-Api-Key` seam, while the contract and the functional design now require Cognito JWT auth. That is an accepted drift the person already saw, but anyone reading these documents today would be misled, so it should be refreshed. With one Major and three Minor findings, the stage meets READY.
